_meta.generator: Claude Code autonomous prep session — queried NotebookLM Lit Review
_meta.todo: PubMed URLs are incomplete — Brian should run each study through pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ and paste the PMID link. Confirmed URLs are marked verified:true; unverified URLs are placeholders.

claims.claim: Eating protein and vegetables before carbohydrates reduces postprandial glucose by approximately 29% at 30 minutes in patients with Type 2 diabetes.
claims.use_when: any output recommending food sequencing; flagship claim for the Food Sequencing Card

claims.claim: A carbohydrate-last food order produced up to a 54% reduction in the incremental glucose peak in adults with prediabetes.
claims.use_when: Food Sequencing Card callout + thumbnail claim for YouTube Short #02

claims.claim: Food sequencing (vegetables before carbohydrates) sustained reductions in HbA1c in patients with type 2 diabetes over 2.5 years of follow-up.
claims.journal: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
claims.use_when: durability claim — sustained effect of food sequencing over 2.5 years in T2D primary cohort

claims.claim: Semaglutide (2.4 mg) produces 14.9% mean weight loss vs. 2.4% for placebo over 68 weeks.
claims.use_when: context for GLP-1 user flow — why these meds are so prevalent

claims.claim: Lean mass loss during GLP-1 therapy is proportional to standard weight-loss interventions, NOT a pathological muscle-wasting effect caused specifically by the drugs.
claims.use_when: GLP-1 output — counters the 'GLP-1 kills your muscle' myth

claims.claim: Layering strict intentional fasting on top of GLP-1 medications (which already suppress appetite) can increase risks of low energy availability without proportional benefits.
claims.study: Mozaffarian D et al., 2025 (Joint Advisory Review)
claims.use_when: GLP-1 FORK — primary citation for why GLP-1 users get the 12:12 safer window. MUST cite on every GLP-1 output.

claims.claim: Patients who discontinue GLP-1 agonists regain approximately two-thirds of their prior weight loss within one year.
claims.use_when: context for long-term thinking on GLP-1 users — informs 'sustainable habits' framing

claims.claim: Intermittent fasting could harm reproductive health in average-weight females if fasting causes insufficient calorie intake.
claims.use_when: WOMEN'S MODE — primary citation for the hormone-safety warning. MUST cite on every female-user output.

claims.claim: Extreme caloric deficits (which can result from fasting) pose specific nutritional and reproductive concerns for female athletes.
claims.journal: International Society of Sports Nutrition (Position Stand)
claims.use_when: Women's Mode — for users who mark themselves as active/athletes

claims.claim: Time-restricted eating impacts weight loss and metabolic parameters differently depending on compliance and biological sex.
claims.use_when: Women's Mode framing — establishing that sex-differentiated defaults are science-backed

claims.claim: Early time-restricted feeding (6-hour eating window) improves insulin sensitivity, beta-cell responsiveness, blood pressure, and oxidative stress — independent of weight loss.
claims.use_when: experienced users opting for tight windows; NEVER recommend this for GLP-1 or female users in v0

claims.claim: A 10-hour time-restricted eating window reduces body weight, BMI, and abdominal trunk fat in adults with metabolic syndrome without significant lean mass loss.
claims.use_when: beginner to intermediate users — 14:10 / 16:8 windows. Core citation for the default Women's Mode window.

claims.claim: Time-restricted feeding affects approximately 40% of genes across 22 organ systems, indicating heavy ties to circadian rhythm alignment.
claims.use_when: MECHANISTIC framing only — always grade 🟠 Speculative because it's an animal model. Never use as a standalone recommendation.

claims.claim: Calorie restriction with or without time-restricted eating produced virtually identical weight loss in adults with obesity over 12 months.
claims.use_when: HONESTY CALLOUT — the brand stewardship move is 'fasting isn't magic, but it works when it fits your life.' Prevents overclaiming.

claims.claim: Light-intensity walking breaks reduce postprandial glucose by 17% and significantly lower insulin versus prolonged sitting.
claims.use_when: post-meal walking recommendation in output — Strong grade, can be the headline

claims.claim: In adults with type 2 diabetes, three 10-minute post-meal walks reduced postprandial glucose by approximately 12% overall (and 22% after dinner) versus a single 30-minute daily walk.
claims.use_when: specific 'walk after dinner' recommendation — strongest evening-walk evidence

claims.claim: Across a 2023 meta-analysis, post-meal exercise significantly reduced glucose excursions (SMD = 0.55) while pre-meal exercise did not reach significance; benefit attenuates if exercise is delayed past ~29 minutes.
claims.use_when: timing specificity — proves 'walk AFTER meals' over 'walk whenever'

claims.claim: Three 15-minute post-meal brisk walks improved HbA1c from 7.9% to 7.0% over 60 days in T2D patients.
claims.use_when: longer-term outcome claim — gives users a concrete target

claims.claim: Walking immediately after a meal improves glucose metrics significantly; walking 30 minutes after shows no significant effect.
claims.use_when: timing precision — 'walk right after eating, not later'

claims.claim: 3-minute bouts of light walking every 30 minutes over 7 hours reduced glucose iAUC by ~39% and insulin by ~36% in inactive T2D patients.
claims.use_when: for sedentary/office worker users — micro-walk framing

claims.claim: Three 15-minute post-meal brisk walks reduced nighttime central systolic BP and improved nocturnal BP dipping in inactive young women.
claims.use_when: bonus claim for users with BP concerns — specifically female-relevant

claims.claim: Alternate-day fasting (ADF) produces weight loss equivalent to conventional daily calorie restriction, not superior, and features a higher dropout rate.
claims.use_when: DEFLECT ADF recommendation — if a user asks for ADF, the output should say 'evidence shows equivalence, not superiority; try 14:10 first'

claims.claim: An umbrella review of 23 meta-analyses found intermittent fasting reliably lowers fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, waist circumference, and fat mass, with modest improvements in fat-free mass.
claims.use_when: headline benefits claim — the strongest evidence we have that IF 'does something'

claims.claim: 36 hours of fasting had only MODEST effects on human skeletal muscle autophagy — exact timing thresholds in humans remain unknown.
claims.use_when: MYTH DEFLECTION — if a user asks about autophagy, the output should cite THIS not the '16-hour autophagy' myth. The brand stewardship move is honesty about what's actually known.
